title: Fukanzazengi Part 2
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett shares a personal story about learning to observe and settle their angry thoughts through a simple yet powerful analogy involving a jar of water and sparkles, illustrating how this practice can help address complex problems by cultivating awareness and clarity in daily life. This approach encourages us to look beyond our conceptual understanding and instead cultivate awareness of our body and emotions, allowing us to deepen our practice and avoid getting caught up in dualistic thinking. By embracing the imperfections and uncertainties of life, we can find a sense of calm and clarity that is not dependent on external validation or intellectual understanding.
topics: Soto Zen teachings on mindfulness and meditation
Dogen's writing on Chinese Buddhist canon
jar of water and sparkles analogy
Soto Zen emphasis on honoring ancestors
